# cloider_registry (Resource)

A container registry project, where images are pushed to and pulled from as `<url>/<repository>:<tag>`. Push and pull with a `cloider_registry_token`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "cloider_registry" "images" {
  name             = "acme"
  storage_limit_gi = 10
  immutable_tags   = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The project's name, 3 to 63 lower case letters, digits and `-`. Project names are shared by every Cloider account, so it has to be one nobody else has. Changing it replaces the project and its images.

### Optional

- `immutable_tags` (Boolean) Whether pushing over a tag or deleting one is refused, `latest` included. Defaults to `false`.
- `public` (Boolean) Whether anyone may pull its images without a token. Pushing always needs one. Defaults to `false`.
- `storage_limit_gi` (Number) The most GiB its images may take, 1 to 20. A push past it is refused. Defaults to `5`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the project was created, RFC 3339.
- `host` (String) The registry host to `docker login` to.
- `id` (String) The project's id.
- `status` (String) `Ready`, `Failed` or `Terminating`.
- `url` (String) The prefix of every image in the project, `<host>/<name>`.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# A project is imported by its id, see `cloider registry list`
terraform import cloider_registry.images r4t6yu
```
